public_health_question.v: What was the source and course of a human tularemia case after a wildlife biologist cut herself during a harbor seal necropsy?

ev.q: the first known report of tularemia acquired through contact with a marine mammal, and the first detection of F. tularensis in a marine mammal.
Tularemia Associated with Harbor Seal Necropsy — Kitsap County, Washington, October 2023
a previously healthy woman aged 32 years who lived in Kitsap County, Washington was evaluated by a primary care provider
The seal necropsy report documented signs of possible infection of unspecified etiology in thoracic and abdominal organs

equity.level_reason: A single case report; the patient's age and sex are descriptors only, and her occupation is a route of exposure, not social position.

ev.q: a previously healthy woman aged 32 years

notes: A single human case with an animal-source investigation and contact monitoring (no additional cases). Laboratory tests (culture, DFA, PCR, sequencing) only confirm case and animal status, so they are not procedures. The figure of fewer than 10 cases annually in Washington is cited.
